# Aerial Site Mapping

Aerial Site Mapping uses drones equipped with high-resolution cameras and LiDAR to capture detailed topographical data of construction zones. Drones fly predetermined paths, collecting overlapping images and sensor readings that software stitches into 3D maps and models. This process speeds up site surveys, improving accuracy compared to manual methods.

Tradeoffs include battery life limiting flight time (typically 20 minutes per drone), weather sensitivity, and data processing requirements. For example, mapping a 5-acre site requires 3 drone flights, producing 3000 images and 15 GB of raw data, processed over 4 hours.

Common failures involve GPS signal loss causing inaccurate positioning, poor lighting affecting image quality, and data stitching errors leading to map distortions. Mitigation requires careful flight planning and robust post-processing algorithms.
